title: Fraction quarrel not fundamental; precarious readings of 'he broke' and 'do this'
pass_a_gloss: That the DISSENT is not fundamental, after the declaration made by the Rinteln men (above p. 336), the Cassel theologians have acknowledged. But the Brethren SUPPOSE: (1) That in the Words of Institution "he broke" is the same as "he distributed," just as in Hebrew פרס and שבר mean to break and also to distribute — as if Christ had used those words, which also come especially in the sense of breaking and dividing; or as if a double action of Christ were not recorded, ἔκλασε καὶ ἐδίδου ("he broke and he gave"), even in the Syriac interpreter; or as if τὸ κλάσαι / κλᾶσθαι were used of bread otherwise than in the sense of breaking in the obvious places of the New Testament. (2) That the breaking is not a necessary matter, because perhaps the manner in which Christ broke is unknown — by which very plea neither εὐλογῆσαι / εὐχαριστῆσαι ("to bless / to give thanks") would be necessary, etc., because the manner is not expressed, though the thing is most expressly stated. (3) That no command stands in the Words "Do this" — namely, what I did — though Luther himself referred those words to the breaking of bread; his words from Jena Works vol. II p. 25 you have in Massonius, Anatomy Part IV p. 253, and in Wendelin, Theological Exercises against Gerhard, Part I, Exercise XVII. See also the consensus of Chemnitz, Mentzer, and the Giessen men in the same Massonius at the place cited.
pass_b_english: After the Rinteln declaration (above, p. 336), the Cassel men grant that this dissent is not fundamental.

Yet the brethren lean on precarious props. First: that in the words of institution "he broke" means only "he distributed," as Hebrew words for breaking can also mean distributing — as if Christ had used those Hebrew words; as if a double act were not recorded, "he broke and he gave" (ἔκλασε καὶ ἐδίδου), even in the Syriac; as if "to break" of bread meant anything else in the plain New Testament places.

Second: that breaking is unnecessary because we may not know how Christ broke — which would also make blessing and giving thanks unnecessary, since the manner is not spelled out, though the act itself is stated as plainly as can be.

Third: that "Do this" carries no command to do what He did — though Luther himself tied those words to the breaking of bread (Jena Works II.25; Massonius Anatomy IV.253; Wendelin against Gerhard, Exercises I.XVII).
See also Chemnitz, Mentzer, and the Giessen consensus in Massonius at the same place. Here Controv. XIII on rites closes before the mutual-tolerance head and before the Hexades.
source_text: DISSENSUM non esse fundamentalem, post declarationem factam à Rintelensibus, suprâ pag. 336. agnoverunt Cassellani. SUPPONUNT autem Fratres, 1. Idem esse in Verbis Instit. fregit, quod distribuit, quomodo פרס & שבר Hebraeis sit frangere & quoque distribuere: Quasi verò aut Christus his vocibus usus sit, quae etiam praecipuè frangendi & dividendi significatu veniunt; aut non duplex actio Christi memoretur ἔκλασε καὶ ἐδίδου, etiam apud Syrum interpretem; aut τὸ κλάσαι, vel κλᾶσθαι, aliter de pane usurpetur, quam sensu frangendi obviis locis Novi Test. 2. Rem non esse necessariam, fractionem, quia fortè nescitur modus quô Christus fregerit; Quo ipso nec necessarium εὐλογῆσαι, εὐχαριστῆσαι, &c. quia non exprimitur modus, re expressissimâ. 3. Mandatum non exstare in Verbis, Hoc facite, scil. quod feci: Quae tamen ad panis fractionem retulit ipse Lutherus, cujus verba ex Tomo II. Oper. Jen. p. 25. habes apud Massonium, Anatom. P. IV. p. 253. & Wendelinum Exercit. Theologicar. contrà Gerhardum, P. I. Exercit. XVII. Vide & Consensum Chemnitii, Mentzeri, Giessensium, apud eundem Massonium, loco cit.
notes: Controv. print pp. 74-75 / PDF ~175-176. Dissensus non fundamentalis after Rinteln; SUPPONUNT 1-3 close. Natural end of Controv. XIII De Ritibus before De Tolerantia mutua (XV) and Hexades Annotationum.
